in_hebrew.name: פietro
in_hebrew.meaning: פטרוס, השם פטרו, נגזר מפטרוס, שפירושו אבן או סלע
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פטרו, נגזר מהמילה היוונית פטרוס (Petros), שפירושו אבן או סלע. זהו שם שמקורו בברית החדשה, בו היה פטרוס אחד מתלמידיו של ישוע, וגם האפיפיור הראשון של הכנסייה הנוצרית. השם פטרו משויך לחוזק, אמינות ומנהיגות.

in_greek.name: Πιέτρο
in_greek.meaning: Πέτρος, το όνομα Πετρος, σημαίνει πέτρα ή βράχος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Πετρος, προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη πέτρα (petra), που σημαίνει πέτρα ή βράχος. Ο Πέτρος ήταν ένας από τους μαθητές του Ιησού και ο πρώτος Πάπας της Χριστιανικής Εκκλησίας. Το όνομα Πέτρος συμβολίζει τη δύναμη, την αξιοπιστία και την ηγετική θέση.

in_latin.name: Pietro
in_latin.meaning: Petrus, nomen Petrus, significat petra vel rupes
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Petrus, derivatum a voce Graeca Petros, significat petra vel rupes. Petrus fuit unus ex discipulis Iesu et primus Papa Ecclesiae Christianae. Nomen Petrus coniungitur cum fortitudine, fidelitate et ductu.

in_english.name: Pietro

in_english.long_meaning: The name Pietro originates from the Greek word 'Petros', meaning rock or stone. It is associated with Saint Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles and the first Pope of the Christian Church. Pietro symbolizes strength, stability, and leadership. The name has been popularized in various Christian cultures, reflecting its biblical significance and historical importance.

biblical_reference.note: Jesus gives Peter the name Cephas (Aramaic) or Petros (Greek), meaning 'rock', on which he will build his church.

data.cultural_impact: Pietro is the Italian name for Peter, one of Jesus's twelve apostles. Throughout history, Pietro has held immense cultural significance as a symbol of loyalty, stability, and leadership. He is often depicted in art and literature as strong, steadfast, and unwavering in his faith. Pietro's leadership helped shape the Christian church and establish it as a powerful global institution.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Pietro represents the foundation upon which the church is built. He is considered the rock upon which Jesus built His church (Matthew 16:18). Pietro's name reflects his spiritual steadfastness and his unwavering faith in Jesus. Pietro's story of denying Jesus three times and being forgiven by Jesus is a powerful reminder of the forgiving nature of God and the importance of confession and repentance. Pietro's name continues to inspire Christians around the world to remain steadfast in their faith and to seek forgiveness and renewal in their relationship with God.

historical_references.reference: Pietro della Vida (c. 1350-1423): A Florentine humanist and biographer, who wrote a comprehensive biography of Petrarch in 1436, which is an essential source for understanding Petrarch's life and influence. He referred to Petrarch as 'Pietro di Dante' and 'Pietro Olivetano' to honor his Tuscan origins and his association with the Olivetan Order.

Pietro Mascagni (1867-1945): An Italian composer known for his operas, including 'Cavalleria Rusticana' and 'Iris', which were popular in the late 19th century. He was born in Livorno, Italy, and was named after his father, also named Pietro.
